lines.text: name: to-tickets

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in a local file, or native blocking links on a real tracker.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: disable-model-invocation: true

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # To Tickets

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Process

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 1. Gather context

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 3. Draft vertical slices

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: <vertical-slice-rules>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Any prefactoring should be done first

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: </vertical-slice-rules>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 4. Quiz the user

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Title**: short descriptive name

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Ask the user:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Should any tickets be merged or split further?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Local files** → write one `tickets.md` in the repo root, all tickets in dependency order (blockers first), each with its "Blocked by" listing the titles it depends on. Use the file template below.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: <tickets-file-template>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Tickets: <short name of the work>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A one-line summary of what these tickets build. Reference the source spec if there is one.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## <Ticket title>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Blocked by:** the titles of the tickets that gate this one, or "None — can start immediately".

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [ ] Acceptance criterion 1

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [ ] Acceptance criterion 2

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## <Ticket title>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: </tickets-file-template>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: <issue-template>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Parent

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## What to build

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not layer-by-layer implementation.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Acceptance criteria

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [ ] Criterion 1

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - [ ] Criterion 2

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Blocked by

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: </issue-template>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: In either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Work the frontier one ticket at a time with `/implement`, clearing context between tickets.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: </content>
